characterList.description: A man in his 40s with short, dark hair, wearing a blue NASA hoodie and blue jeans. He appears friendly and enthusiastic about astrophotography.
characterList.name: Glenn (Astrobloke)

content_metadata.description: A video showcasing Glenn's modifications to his astrophotography rig and a collaboration project, culminating in the presentation of a final HOO image of the Flying Bat and Squid Nebula.

qAndA.answer: He moved the guide scope from the top of the telescope to the bottom, using a dovetail plate.
qAndA.question: What is the main change Glenn made to the placement of his guide scope?

qAndA.answer: He initially spun the EAF so the manual controls were at the bottom for aesthetic reasons, but later reversed it for better balance and clearance.
qAndA.question: Why did Glenn change the orientation of the EAF (Electronic Auto Focuser)?

qAndA.answer: He initially used a long silicone cable with a cigarette plug, but later switched to a shorter cable powered directly from the Pegasus power box.
qAndA.question: What type of cable did Glenn use to power the EQ6-R Pro mount?

qAndA.answer: He is using NINA (Nighttime Imaging 'N' Astronomy) software.
qAndA.question: What software is Glenn using to control his imaging sequence?

qAndA.answer: The final image is a HOO image, which means it was processed using data captured through Hydrogen-alpha, Oxygen III, and Oxygen III filters.
qAndA.question: What kind of image processing technique was used for the final nebula image?

youtube_description:
The Flying Bat and Squid Nebula. A collaboration project taking 93hrs of HOO data. Astrophotography

#Astrobloke #Astrophotography #astronomy 
https://www.youtube.com/c/Astrobloke?sub_confirmation=1

James of DSO imager and Joe of Joe's Astrophoto and myself collaborated on this target and collected a whopping 93 hrs of data. The Squid Nebula that sits inside the Flying bat is a very faint Oxygen III object and needs lots of data to get it to stand out and show its beauty.
We worked on this for quite some time and James did a fantastic final edit of all the data which I show in this video.
Please check out their channels for other great content.
